item.title: We ate nothing but single-grain risotto for a week
item.dc:creator: Sam Brine
item.description: The single-grain risotto takes four hours and tastes like it took three. The single-grain risotto takes four hours and tastes like it took three.
item.content:encoded:
The recipe calls for patience, and then rather more minimal plating.

Purists insist minimal plating peaked in 1974 and has been coasting since.

Restaurants report the single-grain risotto sells best to people who did not order it.
